Fair questions.

Small, cheap, drop-in friendly, phones away. That’s the whole rulebook.

Do I have to come every week?

No. Come when you can. Your usual spot is held, and you tap “can’t make this one” if you’re out. Regulars aren’t signed up for anything. They’re just the people who kept coming back.

Is it the same people every time?

Mostly. A core of regulars forms on its own, and new people join any week. That mix is the point: familiar enough to get to know people, open enough that it never goes stale.

Can I come alone?

Most people do. The host says hi, puts you on a court, and introduces you around. Nobody has to break the ice from zero.

What if I’m not very good?

Levels are mixed on purpose. The host rotates partners so games stay fair and nobody sits out all night.

How much is it?

About your share of the court, plus a small cut for the host who runs it. Food after is pay-your-own and optional (but don’t skip it).

Is this a dating app?

No. No swiping, no profiles to browse. A game, a small group, and something to eat after. The app books you in and then goes quiet. Phones away on court.
